newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks set for volatile week, eye Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks set for volatile week, eye Wall Street.

text.p: The London stock market is likely to remain volatile next week as investors fret that Wall Street may be on the verge of a long-awaited setback.

The FTSE 100, which closed at a record high of 4,271.5 on Thursday, remains under the Dow's spell and any U.S. downturn would almost certainly feed through to UK share prices, dealers and strategists said.
"The market feels there is going to be a U.S. correction but it may not start just yet," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
"I suspect both the U.S. and UK markets will have a breather but volatility will rule."
The trader noted that over the past few months, the Dow has regularly fallen 50 to 100 points in a day, only to recover the lost ground and reach record highs.
"Wall Street's raging bull is a hard animal to stop. It may run out of steam temporarily but with so many strategists still expecting more gains it is dangerous to stand in its way.
"You could get run over."
Dealers noted reports that U.S. investment strategist Elaine Garzarelli had turned bullish on the shares, expecting U.S. stocks to gain 10-15 percent in the next 12-months.

Garzarelli, best known for advising clients to liquidate stocks before the stockmarket crash of 1987, turned bearish on the Dow in July last year but according to market sources is advising clients to buy, citing lower interest rates and strong corporate earnings.
Richard Jeffrey, strategist at Charterhouse Tilney believes the FTSE has not yet seen its 1997 peak but is pessimistic about the market over the final six months of the year.

"I think London will move further up this year. But I still feel the market will find it difficult to defend this high ground in the second half," Jeffrey said. "I think the market is in for a nasty shock later this year."

Jeffrey expects the FTSE to touch the 4,440 level before inflationary pressures and growing consumer spending push interest rates higher, resulting in a modest downturn back to the 4,000 area but year-end.
Corey Miller, strategist at Credit Lyonnais Laing expects the FTSE to consolidate over the next few weeks before resuming an upward trend.
"Fundamentally we are still bullish of the UK market," Miller said, citing strong corporate earnings and historically low interest rates for the upbeat stance.
But a gradual increase in UK base rates is likely to cap the FTSE's run at the 4,450 level, Miller said.
Monday's fourth-quarter gross domestic product(GDP) figures will be closely watched for clues on near-term rates policy, Miller said.

UK Q4 GDP is forecast to rise by 0.7 percent, taking the year-on-year total to 2.6 percent, from 2.4 percent. A significantly higher figure would add fuel to the argument for a near-term hike in UK base rates, as advocated by Bank of England governor Eddie George.
Also on the economic calendar next week are U.S. consumer confidence, durable goods, and real GDP data as well as UK consumer credit, trade, and M4 lending statistics.
Only a handful of second-line UK corporates are due to report, with WH Smith the most significant of the group.
